title: 2.4.30 Triangle of Stars
description: Use a nested loop to print a triangle of stars, one row at a time, where the inner loop's limit depends on the outer loop's counter. Auto-graded.
sourceRef: book 2.4.6: Try It Now 2.4.4 + Concepts in Practice 'Counting nested work'

steps.title: Outer loop: the rows
steps.instructions: Write an outer for loop with counter row running from 1 to 5.

steps.title: Inner loop: bound by row, not a fixed number
steps.instructions: Inside the outer loop, declare an empty string called line. Write an inner for loop with counter star that runs from 1 up to row (not a fixed number like 5): that is what makes each row longer than the last. Append a "*" to line on every inner pass.

steps.title: Print the row
steps.instructions: After the inner loop closes, log line. You should see 1 star on the first line, up to 5 stars on the last.

planChart.mermaid:
flowchart LR
  A([Start]) --> B[row starts at 1]
  B --> C{row is 5 or less}
  C -- yes --> D[make line empty, star starts at 1]
  D --> E{star is up to row}
  E -- yes --> F[add a star to line]
  F --> E
  E -- no --> G[/log line/]
  G --> H[go to the next row]
  H --> C
  C -- no --> I([End])

requirements.title: outer loop present
requirements.description: An outer for loop (1 to 5) contains an inner for loop whose upper bound is the outer loop's own counter, and the row is logged after the inner loop closes. Help: 2.4.24 (Nested Loops)

requirements.title: inner loop bound depends on row
requirements.description: The inner loop's condition compares its own counter to the outer loop's counter, not to a fixed number (any consistent counter names accepted, e.g. i/j). Help: 2.4.24 (Nested Loops)
